settings.description:
Which agent CLI a new agent runs when neither the agent nor its workflow
names one. It has to be a harness this binary implements, so it is one of

Whether `komrad open` sets up a workflow for the git checkout it is run in, with a

Edit the panel's text fields the way vim does. A form's field opens in insert mode, esc goes
to normal mode, and a second esc closes it. The filter, search and rename lines close on esc,
and ctrl+f puts one in normal mode, after which esc works as it does in a form.
Flags appended to every agent's command line for this CLI, ahead of the flags that agent carries itself.

Records each agent's directory as trusted in this CLI's own config when on,
before launching it. The CLI asks whether a directory is trusted the first
time it runs there and waits for an answer, which it reads only from that
file, so an agent in a fresh worktree otherwise starts blocked and shows
here as waiting. Turning this on edits that file on your behalf.
Flags appended to every agent's command line for this CLI, ahead of the flags that agent carries itself.

Records each agent's directory as trusted in this CLI's own config when on,

sections.description:
The review screen, which draws a task's diff in the stage and its review
threads in the sidebar.

settings.description:
From the menu, pass a held comment from the forge on to the writer, copied as your own words and
released at once. A comment is held when its author cannot push to the repository, and the
writer reads nothing in its thread until the comment opening it is accepted.

From the menu, show only the change that answered the comment under the cursor, from the work as
it stood just before the writer's addressed reply to the work that reply carried, or
go back to all changes from there.

Walk back a review, from the whole change to the work since your last review and on into the
older ones, stopping on the oldest.
Walk the other way through your reviews, towards the newest work and on to the whole change.

From the menu, write a message on the line under the cursor, replying in the thread already there
or opening a new one.

From the menu, open the file under the cursor in your editor, beside the diff, on the line the
cursor is on. This is the task's own worktree rather than a copy of it, so what
you write is what the writer finds there, and the key is refused while the writer is
working rather than letting you both write at once. It is drawn off on a range ending
before the newest snapshot, since those lines have moved on.

From the menu, throw away a reply of yours the forge refused on the thread under the cursor. Nothing is
posted.
From the menu, try again with a reply of yours the forge refused on the thread under the cursor.

From the menu, write a reply on the forge thread under the cursor, posted on the pull request where
anyone can read it.

From the menu, jump from the comment under the cursor to the diff it was written against, with the
cursor on it, or back to where you were from there. Anywhere else, move to the next
comment from the forge on the pull request.
Jump to the next line carrying a review thread.
Move the cursor to the next comment nobody has settled. It stops on the last one.
Move the cursor to the previous comment nobody has settled. It stops on the first one.
Jump to the previous line carrying a review thread.
From the menu while the diff ends before the newest snapshot, end it on the newest snapshot.

From the menu, catch up with the writer, taking a snapshot of the worktree as it stands and ending
the diff on it.

From the menu, hide the conversations agents opened, or show them again. They show whenever a
review opens.
From the menu, settle the thread under the cursor, which marks it resolved without deleting it.

On the file tree, open the folder the cursor rests on, or close it when it is open. Over the
file tree, open the review of a task in the stack, go to a thread that needs you, or open the
pull request's description.

From the menu, fold away the file the cursor is in once you have read it, or open it again. A file
the writer writes to afterwards comes back on its own.

sections.description:
Sets where komrad finds the scripts a workflow hangs on a moment in its agents' lives, and how long
each may run.

settings.description:
The directory for hooks, which holds one executable file per hook, named after the hook.
A hook is a script or program komrad runs at a moment a workflow names it against, in the
agent's own directory, with agent info in KOMRAD_AGENT as JSON and the moment in
KOMRAD_TRIGGER. Default is ~/.config/komrad/hooks.

The longest a hook may run before komrad stops it and counts it as failed, as a Go duration
such as "60s" or "5m". A hook's own #KOMRAD timeout can ask for less, never more, and a
hook that asks for "none" gets this. A duration komrad cannot read, or one that is not
positive, is refused.

sections.description: Sets where a workflow's generated worktree provisioner creates its worktrees.

settings.description:
Directory that holds generated worktrees, one subdirectory per agent.
Left empty this is ~/.local/state/komrad/worktrees.

sections.description: Controls how komrad reads the git checkouts its agents work in.

settings.description:
SSH hosts that stand in for a forge's web host, each written as "ssh_host=web_host", such
as "ssh.gitlab.example.com=gitlab.example.com". A remote on the SSH host is then matched to
the forge connected for the web host. Write host names only, with no port, scheme or
user. Public aliases such as ssh.github.com and altssh.gitlab.com are already known.

sections.description: Controls how komrad reads the review threads on the pull requests its agents open.

settings.description:
Logins whose review comments are left out of the threads mirrored onto an agent, such as a
CI bot or a code review App. A thread whose every comment is from one of them is not mirrored
at all. Names ignore case.

The largest check log komrad keeps, in bytes. Komrad drops a log past it, and the panel links to it
on the forge instead. Komrad refuses a negative size.

sections.description: The GitHub App an engine fetches and pushes as.

settings.description:
The App's own id, from its settings page. Left empty the engine has no GitHub identity
and git is left to whatever credentials the account already has, which on a machine
nobody logs into is none.

The installation the token is for, which scopes it to the repositories the App was
installed on rather than to everything it could reach. GitHub writes it as a number, and
it appears in the URL of the installation's own settings page.

The PEM the App was created with. On a deployed engine, komrad fetches this into a tmpfs at
boot rather than writing it to disk, so the key does not outlive the machine.

sections.description: The standing text every agent is started with, whatever workflow it is in.

settings.description:
The file holding global context, read at each launch.
Left empty this is ~/.config/komrad/context.md, but will not trigger a failure if left blank.

sections.description: Controls how komrad delivers mail between agents.

settings.description:
The time mail stays deliverable, as a Go duration such as "3h" or "45m". Komrad neither
delivers nor shows mail past it, and keeps the row as a record that it never arrived. A duration komrad cannot read, or one that is not positive, is refused.

The amount of mail two agents may write each other before komrad refuses a send between
them. It counts the pair in both directions over every thread, so opening a new
subject is not a way around it. When a send is refused komrad marks a row for
attention and tells the recipient its mail was stopped, so an exchange that is cut
off does not leave the other side waiting on a reply that will never arrive. A
negative limit is refused.

sections.description:
The identity provider people sign in to this engine with, and the listener their requests
reach it on.

settings.description:
The provider's issuer, like https://accounts.google.com, which every ID token it signs
names. Left empty, along with client_id, the engine takes no signed-in requests.

The id the owner registered komrad under at the provider, which every ID token for komrad
names as its audience.

The secret some providers, such as Google, hand a desktop app beside its id. Every copy of
komrad carries it, so it protects nothing, and `komrad login` reads it from the engine.

The address the public listener serves signed-in requests on. It has to be a loopback
host, since a web server on the same machine carries the network's requests to it.

sections.description: Which komrad this is, by its database, its address, its tmux socket and its cache.

settings.description:
The Postgres komrad keeps every agent, workflow, schedule and transcript in, reached as
this engine's own login, which is what keeps its rows apart from every other engine's.
`komrad engine ensure` creates the login and prints this url.
Left empty this is the default engine's login on the embedded Postgres under state_dir.
Whenever this reaches the socket under state_dir, the server runs the embedded Postgres and
starts it again when it exits.

The login that owns the schema, used only by `komrad migrate` and the `komrad engine` commands.
Left empty this is database_url, or the embedded Postgres's owner while database_url reaches it.

The least-privilege login the MCP query tools connect as.
Left empty this is database_url with the engine's reader login, which is its own login
with _reader on the end and the same password.

The address the server listens on, which the panel, the CLI and the MCP
endpoint all reach it at. Change it to run two komrads on one machine. It has to be a
loopback host, since the api has no auth and its writes spawn agents.

The tmux socket komrad runs its own server on. Nothing in your normal tmux sees
that server, which is why `tmux -L komrad ls` is how you look at it directly.

The directory where komrad keeps what it generates, such as the server log, the built-in
scripts it writes out on every start, and the temp files a harness passes a prompt through.
Left empty this is ~/Library/Caches/komrad on a Mac and ~/.cache/komrad on Linux.
Everything under it is komrad's to delete and rewrite, so nothing of yours belongs here.

The directory where komrad keeps its own files about agents, such as generated worktrees,
released reviews and forge credentials.
Left empty this is ~/.local/state/komrad.
It holds credentials and is komrad's to manage, so nothing of yours belongs here.

The https address the engine is served on, like https://komrad.example.com. Left empty the
engine is local and an agent's terminal is shown by moving its own pane into the panel. It
may be plain http when its host is this machine.
